title: Who Will Be the Next Prime Minister of the UK?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: The head of government in a parliamentary system, responsible for leading the country and the government.
A politician who has been elected to represent a constituency in the House of Commons.
The act of officially leaving an important job or position.
A public vote in which citizens decide an important political question directly.
A government policy of reducing public spending to lower debt.
The geographical area that an MP represents in parliament.
The transfer of political powers from a national government to regional or local governments.

sentences.en: In 2024, Keir Starmer became the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after leading the Labour Party to one of the biggest election victories in modern British history.
sentences.zh: 2024年，Keir Starmer领导工党在现代英国历史上取得了最大的一次大选胜利，随后出任英国首相。

sentences.en: Just two years later, he has announced his resignation… and Britain is once again preparing for a new leader.
sentences.zh: 仅仅两年后，他便宣布辞职……英国再次迎来了新领袖的筹备期。

sentences.en: Since the Brexit referendum in 2016, the UK has gone through an unusually high number of prime ministers.
sentences.zh: 自2016年脱欧公投以来，英国经历的首相更换频率高得异常。

sentences.en: Each has promised to solve the country’s problems, but then ended up leaving their role earlier than expected.
sentences.zh: 每一位首相上台时都承诺解决国家的问题，但最后都比预期更早地卸任了。

sentences.en: In fact, this is now the third time I’ve made an episode asking the question, “Who Will Be the Next Prime Minister of the UK?” Episode 161 explored the race to replace Boris Johnson back in 2022, and Episode 302 looked at what might happen if the Conservatives lost power before the 2024 election.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这已经是我第三次做关于“谁将成为下一任英国首相？”的播客节目了。第161集探讨了2022年接替Boris Johnson的竞选，而第302集则关注了如果保守党在2024年大选前失利会发生什么。

sentences.en: We’re asking exactly the same question again in this episode, but this time, it’s the Labour Party looking for a new leader.
sentences.zh: 我们在这一集里问的还是完全相同的问题，但这一次，轮到工党在物色新领袖了。

sentences.en: So, what happened? Why has Keir Starmer resigned after such a convincing election victory?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟发生了什么？为什么Keir Starmer在取得如此令人信服的大选胜利后会辞职呢？

sentences.en: Who is Andy Burnham, the politician many people expect to replace him?
sentences.zh: 许多人预计将接替他的政治人物Andy Burnham是谁？

sentences.en: What kind of prime minister might he become?
sentences.zh: 他可能会成为一个什么样的首相？

sentences.en: And why has British politics become so unstable over the past decade?
sentences.zh: 为什么过去十年里英国政治会变得如此不稳定？

sentences.en: Let’s find out, and at the same time learn some new English vocabulary and practice your English listening comprehension.
sentences.zh: 让我们一探究竟，同时学习一些新的英语词汇，并练习你的英语听力理解。

sentences.en: When Keir Starmer led Labour to victory in the 2024 general election, many people thought Britain had entered a new political era.
sentences.zh: 当Keir Starmer领导工党赢得2024年大选时，许多人以为英国已经进入了一个新的政治时代。

sentences.en: After 14 years of Conservative governments, Labour won a huge parliamentary majority.
sentences.zh: 在经历了14年的保守党政府之后，工党赢得了巨大的议会多数席位。

sentences.en: Actually, here I should probably say that in the UK, instead of saying the Conservative Party or the Labour Party or the Liberal Democratic Party, we like to abbreviate it to just Conservatives, Labour, Lib Dems, Reform, Greens.
sentences.zh: 说实话，在这里我可能应该说明一下，在英国，我们不喜欢说“保守党”、“工党”、“自由民主党”，而是喜欢简称为“Conservatives”、“Labour”、“Lib Dems”、“Reform”、“Greens”。

sentences.en: So we like to abbreviate our political parties.
sentences.zh: 所以我们喜欢把政党名称进行简写。

sentences.en: Keir Starmer won the election in 2024 for Labour, and he promised that he was going to deliver change.
sentences.zh: Keir Starmer代表工党赢得了2024年的大选，他承诺将带来变革。

sentences.en: He was going to bring back trust in British politics, and maybe bring back some stability to the country.
sentences.zh: 他要重塑英国政治的信任，或许还要给这个国家带回一些稳定性。

sentences.en: Since 2016, UK politics has been a mess.
sentences.zh: 自2016年以来，英国政治一直一团糟。

sentences.en: It’s been struggling with arguments about Brexit, economic issues and inflation, and then various different political scandals.
sentences.zh: 它一直在与关于脱欧的争论、经济问题和通货膨胀，以及各种不同的政治丑闻作斗争。

sentences.en: And Keir Starmer did have some success. He introduced more rights for workers, he strengthened the UK’s immigration system, and introduced more support for children.
sentences.zh: 而且Keir Starmer确实取得了一些成功。他为工人引入了更多权利，加强了英国的移民系统，并为儿童提供了更多支持。

sentences.en: But he is resigning, after less than two years.
sentences.zh: 但他却在不到两年的时间里宣布辞职了。

sentences.en: Why? There wasn’t one single event that has caused Starmer to resign.
sentences.zh: 为什么？并没有单一事件导致Starmer辞职。

sentences.en: Unlike previous prime ministers, including Boris Johnson, whose leadership was damaged by the Partygate scandal, or Liz Truss, who had terrible economic policies that caused chaos, Starmer’s downfall, Starmer’s path to resigning, was slower.
sentences.zh: 不像之前的首相，比如因“聚会门”丑闻而声誉受损的Boris Johnson，或者因糟糕的经济政策引发混乱的Liz Truss，Starmer的下台、他走向辞职的过程要缓慢得多。

sentences.en: It was the result of different problems that gradually built up.
sentences.zh: 这是一系列逐渐积聚的不同问题所导致的后果。

sentences.en: The biggest challenge was the economy. When Labour came to power, when Labour was elected, they inherited an economy that had experienced years of slow growth.
sentences.zh: 最大的挑战是经济。当工党掌权、工党当选时，他们接手的是一个经历多年缓慢增长的经济体。

sentences.en: The UK has high public debt, and our public services have been struggling.
sentences.zh: 英国公共债务高企，我们的公共服务一直步履维艰。

sentences.en: The previous conservative governments followed a policy known as austerity.
sentences.zh: 前保守党政府奉行被称为“紧缩政策”的方针。

sentences.en: Austerity is an economic policy where governments cut spending and sometimes raise taxes to reduce debt.
sentences.zh: 紧缩政策是一种经济政策，即政府削减开支，有时还会加税以减少债务。

sentences.en: So after years of austerity under conservative governments, many voters voted for Labour because they wanted more investment in healthcare, transport, housing, public services.
sentences.zh: 因此，在保守党政府多年的紧缩政策之后，许多选民投票给工党是因为他们希望加大对医疗保健、交通、住房和公共服务的投资。

sentences.en: They wanted the government to stop cutting spending and to start spending more.
sentences.zh: 他们希望政府停止削减开支，转而增加花销。

sentences.en: But Starmer’s government had issues. Basically, there wasn’t enough money to do everything that people wanted without borrowing more money or raising taxes.
sentences.zh: 但Starmer的政府也存在问题。说白了，如果不借更多的钱或者加税，就没有足够的资金去做人们想要的一切事情。

sentences.en: So Labour often appeared quite cautious.
sentences.zh: 因此工党往往显得相当谨慎。

sentences.en: They didn’t seem very ambitious. Several government decisions were very unpopular as well.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来并没有什么雄心壮志。几项政府决策也极不受欢迎。

sentences.en: Labour supporters were angered by plans to reform disability benefits.
sentences.zh: 工党支持者对改革残疾人福利的计划感到愤怒。

sentences.en: The government was criticized for their plans to change certain benefits for old people.
sentences.zh: 政府因改变老年人某些福利的计划而受到批评。

sentences.en: And then there were some big political controversies.
sentences.zh: 接着还发生了一些重大的政治争议。

sentences.en: Starmer was criticized for accepting gifts from wealthy donors, and his decision to appoint Peter Mandelson as Britain’s ambassador to the United States was really criticized because Mandelson was quite associated with the infamous Jeffrey Epstein.
sentences.zh: Starmer因接受富裕捐赠者的礼物而受到批评，而他任命Peter Mandelson为英国驻美国大使的决定更是饱受诟病，因为Mandelson与臭名昭著的杰弗里·爱泼斯坦（Jeffrey Epstein）关系密切。

sentences.en: None of these issues alone would be enough to force a prime minister to resign, but together they contributed to a feeling that Starmer’s government, that the Labour government, was in trouble.
sentences.zh: 这些问题单独拿出来都不足以迫使一位首相辞职，但它们加在一起，让人觉得Starmer的政府、工党政府陷入了困境。

sentences.en: Starmer never had a political identity. Margaret Thatcher had Thatcherism.
sentences.zh: Starmer从来没有确立自己的政治身份。玛格丽特·撒切尔有撒切尔主义。

sentences.en: Tony Blair had the Third Way. Boris Johnson, even though he wasn’t particularly good as a prime minister, he was associated with the idea of getting Brexit done.
sentences.zh: 托尼·布莱尔有第三条道路。Boris Johnson虽然作为首相并不是特别出色，但他与完成脱欧的理念紧密相连。

sentences.en: Starmer didn’t really have anything. There’s nothing to really think about as a purely Starmer policy.
sentences.zh: Starmer其实什么也没有。没有什么能让人纯粹联想到属于Starmer的政策。

sentences.en: But the biggest blow to Starmer’s government came a few months ago, during the UK’s local elections.
sentences.zh: 但对Starmer政府最大的打击发生在几个月前的英国地方选举期间。

sentences.en: Labour’s results were really disappointing.
sentences.zh: 工党的选举结果非常令人失望。

sentences.en: These were local elections, elections for local town councils or city councils or local mayors.
sentences.zh: 这些是地方选举，也就是选出地方城镇议会、市议会或地方市长的选举。

sentences.en: Labour did not do well. Reform UK, which is the right-wing populist party led by Nigel Farage, performed really well.
sentences.zh: 工党表现不佳。由奈杰尔·法拉奇（Nigel Farage）领导的右翼民粹主义政党“英国改革党”表现相当出色。

sentences.en: So pressure was growing on Starmer. Eventually, he accepted that many of his own MPs, many of his own Members of Parliament, no longer trusted him to lead the Labour Party.
sentences.zh: 因此，给Starmer施加的压力越来越大。最终，他接受了现实，承认他自己的许多议员、许多本党议员不再信任他来领导工党。

sentences.en: He announced that he would resign as both Labour leader and prime minister once his successor, the next leader of Labour Party, had been chosen.
sentences.zh: 他宣布，一旦选出他的继任者——工党的新领袖，他将辞去工党领袖和首相职务。

sentences.en: Here is an important point to remember, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这里有一个需要记住的重要观点。

sentences.en: Labour has a large majority in Parliament and Britain is not holding an election.
sentences.zh: 工党在议会中拥有多数席位，而且英国目前没有举行大选。

sentences.en: The UK is a parliamentary political system.
sentences.zh: 英国是一个议会制政治体系。

sentences.en: It’s not a presidential political system.
sentences.zh: 它不是总统制政治体系。

sentences.en: This means to choose the next prime minister, the Labour Party simply chooses a new leader, and the new leader of the Labour Party will automatically become prime minister because Labour controls Parliament.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要选出下一任首相，工党只需选出一位新领袖，而这位工党新领袖由于工党控制了议会，将自动成为首相。

sentences.en: You can find out more about the difference between prime ministers and presidents in my bonus episode that I will be releasing on Friday, so later this week.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我周五（也就是本周晚些时候）发布的加更节目中了解更多关于首相和总统区别的信息。

sentences.en: That’s on Patreon if you’re interested. But this brings us to the man who is almost guaranteed to take over from Keir Starmer as prime minister: Andy Burnham.
sentences.zh: 如果你感兴趣的话，那期节目在Patreon上。但这让我们想到了几乎铁定接替Keir Starmer出任首相的那个人：Andy Burnham。

sentences.en: Andy Burnham was born in Liverpool in 1970 and then grew up in Cheshire, close to Liverpool.
sentences.zh: Andy Burnham 1970年出生于利物浦，随后在靠近利物浦的柴郡长大。

sentences.en: He has often said that he became interested in politics as a teenager after watching a BBC drama called Boys from the Blackstuff, which focused on unemployment and poverty in Liverpool during the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 他经常说，自己在十几岁时看了BBC一部名为《黑领带男孩》（Boys from the Blackstuff）的电视剧后对政治产生了兴趣，该剧聚焦于20世纪80年代利物浦的失业和贫困问题。

sentences.en: Burnham studied English at the University of Cambridge, but he has spoken about feeling like an outsider there.
sentences.zh: Burnham在剑桥大学学习英语，但他曾坦言在那里觉得自己像个局外人。

sentences.en: In his book called Head North, he described suffering from “imposter syndrome”.
sentences.zh: 在他的书《向北进发》（Head North）中，他描述了自己饱受“冒名顶替综合征”折磨的经历。

sentences.en: Imposter syndrome is the feeling you don’t really belong or deserve your success.
sentences.zh: 冒名顶替综合征是指一种觉得自己并不真正属于这里或不配拥有成功的心理感觉。

sentences.en: After graduating, he worked briefly as a journalist before going into politics.
sentences.zh: 毕业后，他短暂做过记者，随后投身政坛。

sentences.en: He was a parliamentary researcher, then a special advisor, and then he was elected as the Labour MP, the Labour Member of Parliament, for Leigh in Greater Manchester in 2001.
sentences.zh: 他当过议会研究员、特别顾问，然后于2001年当选为大曼彻斯特利（Leigh）选区的工党议员。

sentences.en: He served in several different government positions under Prime Ministers Tony Blair and Gordon Brown.
sentences.zh: 他在首相托尼·布莱尔和戈登·布朗手下担任过多个不同的政府职务。

sentences.en: He was the UK’s Health Secretary and also the Culture Secretary.
sentences.zh: 他曾任英国卫生大臣兼文化大臣。

sentences.en: In 2009, he attended a memorial service marking 20 years since the Hillsborough disaster.
sentences.zh: 2009年，他出席了纪念希尔斯堡惨剧发生20周年的悼念仪式。

sentences.en: Hillsborough was a disaster in which 97 Liverpool football fans lost their lives during a stadium crush in 1989.
sentences.zh: 希尔斯堡惨剧是一场悲剧，在1989年的一场球场踩踏事故中，97名利物浦足球俱乐部球迷失去了生命。

sentences.en: Burnham was loudly heckled by members of the crowd.
sentences.zh: Burnham在现场遭到人群的大声质问和起哄。

sentences.en: Heckled means they shouted at him, they abused him, they booed him.
sentences.zh: 被质问（heckled）的意思是人们对他大喊大叫、辱骂并发出嘘声。

sentences.en: Hillsborough was a seriously controversial issue in the UK, and especially in Liverpool, because many families believed the truth had been covered up for years.
sentences.zh: 希尔斯堡惨剧是英国尤其是利物浦的一个极其具有争议的问题，因为许多家庭认为真相多年来一直被掩盖。

sentences.en: Unlike other politicians, Burnham listened to the criticism.
sentences.zh: 与其他政客不同，Burnham听取了批评意见。

sentences.en: He pushed for another inquiry into the disaster, and many Liverpool supporters and people in Liverpool now credit him with helping keep political pressure on the issue.
sentences.zh: 他大力推动对这场灾难进行另一次调查，许多利物浦球迷和利物浦当地人现在认为是他帮助维持了对该问题的政治压力。

sentences.en: His popularity increased significantly. But despite becoming one of Labour’s most recognizable politicians, Burnham twice failed to become the leader of the party.
sentences.zh: 他的支持率显著上升。但尽管成为了工党辨识度最高的政治人物之一，Burnham却两次竞选党内领袖失败。

sentences.en: After Labour lost the 2010 general election, he stood for the party leadership, but he finished fourth behind Ed Miliband.
sentences.zh: 工党在2010年大选中失利后，他参加了党魁竞选，但在埃德·米利班德（Ed Miliband）之后名列第四。

sentences.en: Five years later, he tried again, but then lost to Jeremy Corbyn, and Jeremy Corbyn’s politics completely transformed Labour.
sentences.zh: 五年后，他再次尝试，但输给了杰里米·科尔宾（Jeremy Corbyn），而杰里米·科尔宾的政治理念彻底改造了工党。

sentences.en: In 2017, he left Westminster to become the directly elected mayor of Greater Manchester.
sentences.zh: 2017年，他离开威斯敏斯特，当选为大曼彻斯特的直选市长。

sentences.en: Actually, Westminster is something called a metonym.
sentences.zh: 其实，威斯敏斯特是一个所谓的转喻词。

sentences.en: A metonym is where we use a place to refer to something bigger.
sentences.zh: 转喻是指我们用一个地方来指代更大的事物。

sentences.en: For example, the White House refers to the President.
sentences.zh: 例如，白宫指代总统。

sentences.en: Wall Street refers to the economic center of New York, the financial district.
sentences.zh: 华尔街指代纽约的经济中心、金融区。

sentences.en: And Westminster refers to the UK Parliament.
sentences.zh: 而威斯敏斯特则指代英国议会。

sentences.en: If you want to refer to the UK government, the civil service, more specifically, you can say Whitehall.
sentences.zh: 如果你想更具体地指代英国政府或文官队伍，你可以说Whitehall（白厅）。

sentences.en: So Westminster and Whitehall. But Burnham left Parliament in 2017, and he went to be the mayor of Manchester.
sentences.zh: 所以是威斯敏斯特和白厅。但Burnham在2017年离开议会，去当了曼彻斯特市长。

sentences.en: This could have been seen as a big step down.
sentences.zh: 这本可能被视为一次大退步。

sentences.en: He left national politics to go and run a city in the north of England.
sentences.zh: 他离开了国家政治，去管理英格兰北部的一座城市。

sentences.en: But it actually strengthened his image, and he wasn’t the only Member of Parliament to go and run a city.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上强化了他的形象，而且他并不是唯一一个去管理城市的议员。

sentences.en: Boris Johnson was a Member of Parliament.
sentences.zh: Boris Johnson曾是一名议员。

sentences.en: He quit to become mayor of London, and he went back to Parliament and became prime minister.
sentences.zh: 他辞职去竞选伦敦市长，后来又重返议会并当选为首相。

sentences.en: Andy Burnham has done something similar.
sentences.zh: Andy Burnham做了类似的事情。

sentences.en: As Mayor of Manchester, Burnham has had quite a good reputation.
sentences.zh: 作为曼彻斯特市长，Burnham赢得了相当不错的声誉。

sentences.en: He’s had a reputation as someone who cared about the problems in the city.
sentences.zh: 他的名声是一个关心这座城市各种问题的人。

sentences.en: His biggest achievement has been the creation of the Bee Network.
sentences.zh: 他最大的成就是创建了“小蜜蜂网络”（Bee Network）。

sentences.en: The Bee Network is an integrated public transport system that combines buses, trams, cycling, and walking.
sentences.zh: 小蜜蜂网络是一个整合了公交、有轨电车、骑行和步行的公共交通系统。

sentences.en: Greater Manchester also became the first area outside of London to bring the bus services back under public control.
sentences.zh: 大曼彻斯特也成为了伦敦以外第一个将公交服务重新收归公共控制的地区。

sentences.en: So instead of being private, they are now publicly owned.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们不再属于私营，而是由公众所有。

sentences.en: He also became really well known during the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 他在新冠疫情期间也变得家喻户晓。

sentences.en: When Boris Johnson’s government introduced lockdowns, Burnham publicly challenged the government over the levels of financial support being offered to towns in northern England.
sentences.zh: 当Boris Johnson政府实施封城时，Burnham就向政府提供的针对英格兰北部城镇的财政支持水平提出了公开性质的质疑。

sentences.en: This earned him the nickname the King of the North.
sentences.zh: 这为他赢得了“北方之王”的绰号。

sentences.en: He was a politician standing up for the north of England.
sentences.zh: 他是一位挺身而出捍卫英格兰北部的政治家。

sentences.en: I mentioned a few minutes ago that Andy Burnham is almost guaranteed to be the next leader of the Labour Party and the next prime minister of the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 我几分钟前提到过，Andy Burnham几乎铁定会成为工党下一任领袖和英国下一任首相。

sentences.en: Of course, things could change after I’ve recorded this episode, but he is almost guaranteed to be the next leader.
sentences.zh: 当然，在我录制完这期节目后情况可能会有变化，但他几乎百分之百是下一任领袖了。

sentences.en: But he can’t do this as the mayor of Manchester.
sentences.zh: 但他不能以曼彻斯特市长的身份做到这一点。

sentences.en: As mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham left Parliament a decade ago, and under Britain’s political system, the prime minister is almost always an MP sitting in the House of Commons.
sentences.zh: 作为大曼彻斯特市长，Burnham十年前就离开了议会，而根据英国的政治体制，首相几乎总是下议院的现任议员。

sentences.en: If Andy Burnham wanted to become Labour Party leader, he would need to get back into Parliament.
sentences.zh: 如果Andy Burnham想成为工党领袖，他需要重返议会。

sentences.en: How could he do this? We don’t have a general election for another three years probably.
sentences.zh: 他怎么做到这一点呢？我们可能还要三年才会迎来大选。

sentences.en: Well, in order to give Burnham a chance to enter Parliament, the Labour MP Josh Simons stepped down from Parliament.
sentences.zh: 好吧，为了给Burnham一个进入议会的机会，工党议员Josh Simons辞去了议员职务。

sentences.en: He stepped down to give Burnham a chance.
sentences.zh: 他辞职是为了给Burnham创造机会。

sentences.en: By stepping down, by quitting, he triggered a by-election in the constituency of Makerfield near Manchester.
sentences.zh: 通过辞职，他引发了曼彻斯特附近马克菲尔德（Makerfield）选区的补选。

sentences.en: A by-election is a special election held to fill a parliamentary seat that becomes vacant, empty, between general elections.
sentences.zh: 补选是为了填补在两次大选之间空缺的议会席位而特别举行的选举。

sentences.en: Instead of the whole country voting, only the people living in that constituency, that area, choose a new MP.
sentences.zh: 不是全国投票，而只有居住在该选区、那个地区的人们来选出新议员。

sentences.en: Burnham was selected as Labour’s candidate, and then he comfortably defeated Reform UK, increasing Labour’s number of votes compared with the last election.
sentences.zh: Burnham被选为工党的候选人，随后他轻松击败了英国改革党，与上次大选相比增加了工党的得票数。

sentences.en: And he returned to Parliament for the first time since 2017.
sentences.zh: 他也自2017年以来首次重返议会。

sentences.en: Just days later, he traveled to Westminster, where he was officially sworn in as the MP for Makerfield.
sentences.zh: 几天后，他前往威斯敏斯特，在那里正式宣誓就任马克菲尔德的议员。

sentences.en: On the same day he became an MP, Keir Starmer resigned.
sentences.zh: 在他成为议员的同一天，Keir Starmer宣布辞职。

sentences.en: Burnham’s position became even stronger when Wes Streeting, who is one of Labour’s most senior politicians and someone widely expected to enter the leadership race himself, endorsed Burnham.
sentences.zh: 随着Wes Streeting的支持，Burnham的地位变得更加巩固。Wes Streeting是工党最高层的政治人物之一，也是原本被广泛预期会参加党魁竞选的人。

sentences.en: To endorse means give your support. This removed his biggest competitor.
sentences.zh: 支持（endorse）的意思是给予背书支持。这消除了他最大的竞争对手。

sentences.en: So now Andy Burnham is a member of Parliament, and he will almost certainly be the next leader of the Labour Party, which means he will be the next Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 所以现在Andy Burnham是一名议员，他几乎铁定会成为工党下一任领袖，这意味着他将成为下一任首相。

sentences.en: What would he be like as a prime minister?
sentences.zh: 他作为首相会是什么样呢？

sentences.en: Well, no one exactly knows what kind of leader a prime minister will be until they take office, until they become the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在一个人上任、成为首相之前，没有人能确切知道他会成为什么样的领袖。

sentences.en: Politicians usually say one thing when they’re campaigning for elections, and then they do something different when they are elected.
sentences.zh: 政客们在竞选时通常说一套，当选后又会做另一套。

sentences.en: But we can make some guesses about what Andy Burnham will focus on as the PM.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以对Andy Burnham作为首相将专注于哪些方面做出一些猜测。

sentences.en: Throughout his time as Mayor of Greater Manchester, he has argued repeatedly that too much power is in London.
sentences.zh: 在他担任大曼彻斯特市长的整个时期，他一再辩称伦敦集中了太多的权力。

sentences.en: He believes that cities and regions in England should have greater control over their transport, housing, education, healthcare, economic plans.
sentences.zh: 他认为英格兰的城市和地区应该在交通、住房、教育、医疗保健、经济计划方面拥有更大的控制权。

sentences.en: If he becomes prime minister, many people think he is going to push for the biggest transfer of political power in decades.
sentences.zh: 如果他成为首相，许多人认为他将推动数十年来最大规模的政治权力下放。

sentences.en: Instead of making every decision in London, his government could give more responsibility and more funding to regional mayors and local authorities, local councils, across England.
sentences.zh: 他的政府可能不会在伦敦做所有决定，而是会赋予英格兰各地的地方市长和地方当局、地方议会更多的责任和资金。

sentences.en: I’m saying England because Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland already have their own power.
sentences.zh: 我之所以说英格兰，是因为苏格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰已经拥有了属于他们自己的权力。

sentences.en: But in England, all of the power is in London.
sentences.zh: 但在英格兰，所有的权力都在伦敦。

sentences.en: In fact, Andy Burnham is likely to be the first prime minister since Harold Wilson in the 1970s to not live at Number 10 Downing Street.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Andy Burnham很可能成为自20世纪70年代的哈罗德·威尔逊（Harold Wilson）以来，第一位不住在唐宁街10号的首相。

sentences.en: Number 10 Downing Street is the traditional home of the prime ministers in Central London.
sentences.zh: 唐宁街10号是伦敦市中心首相的传统住所。

sentences.en: He has said that he’s going to continue living in Wigan in Greater Manchester, and he will split his work week between Manchester and London.
sentences.zh: 他曾表示，他将继续住在是大曼彻斯特的威根（Wigan），并把他的工作周时间在曼彻斯特和伦敦之间分配。

sentences.en: To do this, he has proposed creating a permanent government office in Manchester, nicknamed the Number Ten North.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他提议在曼彻斯特设立一个常设政府办公室，被称为“北方十号”。

sentences.en: This, I think, would actually be quite a welcome change.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这其实会是一个相当受欢迎的改变。

sentences.en: Most of the UK feels that the government focuses far too much on London.
sentences.zh: 英国大部分地区都觉得政府把过多的精力放在了伦敦上。

sentences.en: And Keir Starmer, our most recent prime minister, is from London.
sentences.zh: 而我们最近的一位首相Keir Starmer就来自伦敦。

sentences.en: He was born and raised in London. People perhaps want a non-London focused government.
sentences.zh: 他在伦敦出生并长大。人们或许想要一个不以伦敦为中心的政府。

sentences.en: Another likely thing that Andy Burnham will focus on is probably public services.
sentences.zh: Andy Burnham可能会关注的另一个重点大概是公共服务。

sentences.en: When he was the mayor of Manchester, his biggest creation was the Bee Network, that network that combined cycling and buses and trams and walking.
sentences.zh: 当他担任曼彻斯特市长时，他最大的成就是创建了“小蜜蜂网络”，那个将骑行、公交、有轨电车和步行结合起来的网络。

sentences.en: He could propose similar things in other cities, maybe encourage it nationwide.
sentences.zh: 他可能会在其他城市提出类似的想法，也许会在全国范围内推广。

sentences.en: Rather than talking about economic statistics a lot, Burnham tends to speak about whether people can go to work easily or find affordable homes or receive good healthcare.
sentences.zh: 比起大谈经济数据，Burnham往往更愿意谈论人们是否能轻松去上班、找到负担得起的住房或获得良好的医疗服务。

sentences.en: He seems to be more interested in outcomes than statistics.
sentences.zh: 他似乎对实际结果比对统计数据更感兴趣。

sentences.en: But obviously that could change when he is the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的是，当他成为首相后，这种情况可能会发生变化。

sentences.en: But one thing that will be different is his communication style.
sentences.zh: 不过有一件肯定会不同的是他的沟通风格。

sentences.en: He speaks very differently to some of our previous prime ministers.
sentences.zh: 他的讲话方式与我们之前的某些首相截然不同。

sentences.en: Keir Starmer was very cautious, methodical.
sentences.zh: Keir Starmer非常谨慎、有条不紊。

sentences.en: Before he was prime minister, he was a human rights lawyer.
sentences.zh: 在担任首相之前，他是一名维权律师。

sentences.en: He’s a very lawyer-like prime minister. Burnham is seen as warmer and more emotional.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常具有律师风格的首相。而Burnham则被认为更温暖、更有情绪感染力。

sentences.en: During COVID-19, he became nationally known for challenging Boris Johnson, and he presented himself as someone willing to fight for Manchester.
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情期间，他因公开挑战Boris Johnson而全国闻名，并将自己塑造为一个愿意为曼彻斯特争取利益的人。

sentences.en: Politically, Burnham is what is called a pragmatist.
sentences.zh: 在政治上，Burnham被称为实用主义者。

sentences.en: A pragmatist is a person who focuses on solving problems or making decisions based on real world results rather than theories or ideologies or ideals.
sentences.zh: 实用主义者是指一个专注于根据现实世界的结果而不是理论、意识形态或理想来解决问题或做出决策的人。

sentences.en: You might confuse pragmatism for populism.
sentences.zh: 你可能会把实用主义与民粹主义混淆。

sentences.en: A populist focuses on doing what makes them popular.
sentences.zh: 民粹主义者专注于做那些能让他们受欢迎的事。

sentences.en: Simple answers to difficult questions is the basic definition of a populist.
sentences.zh: 对难题给出简单的答案是民粹主义者的基本定义。

sentences.en: Whereas a pragmatist, like a populist, maybe doesn’t always stick to an ideology, but they’re doing things to solve problems.
sentences.zh: 而实用主义者和民粹主义者一样，也许并不总是死守某种意识形态，但他们做事是为了解决问题。

sentences.en: Earlier in his career, he was associated with Labour’s more moderate or center-right side.
sentences.zh: 在他职业生涯的早期，他曾与工党偏温和或中右翼的一派联系紧密。

sentences.en: But over time, he has supported policies like bringing buses under public control or increasing public investment in local services.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，他支持了诸如将公交收归公有或增加对地方公共服务公共投资等政策。

sentences.en: Some people have criticized him, saying this is a bit populist.
sentences.zh: 有些人批评他，说这有点民粹主义。

sentences.en: But others say, “Well, actually, this was the best solution for Manchester at the time.”
sentences.zh: 但另一些人则说：“嗯，实际上，这是当时对曼彻斯特最好的解决方案。”

sentences.en: Having public services meant that Manchester was in a better situation.
sentences.zh: 拥有公共服务意味着曼彻斯特处于更好的境地。

sentences.en: Of course, Burnham’s going to have challenges.
sentences.zh: 当然，Burnham也将面临挑战。

sentences.en: Britain still faces slow economic growth.
sentences.zh: 英国仍然面临经济增长缓慢的问题。

sentences.en: The public services are struggling across the country, especially our healthcare system.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的公共服务步履维艰，尤其是我们的医疗保健系统。

sentences.en: There’s high government debt, housing shortages, and now the rise of the Reform UK political party.
sentences.zh: 政府债务高企、住房短缺，现在还有英国改革党这一政党的崛起。

sentences.en: And these problems will not be solved overnight.
sentences.zh: 这些问题不可能一夜之间得到解决。

sentences.en: If Andy Burnham does become the prime minister, he will be the seventh Prime Minister of the United Kingdom since the Brexit referendum in 2016.
sentences.zh: 如果Andy Burnham真的成为首相，他将是自2016年脱欧公投以来的第七位英国首相。

sentences.en: That’s unusual for the UK. Margaret Thatcher was prime minister for 11 years.
sentences.zh: 这在英国很不寻常。玛格丽特·撒切尔当了11年首相。

sentences.en: Tony Blair was prime minister for over 10 years.
sentences.zh: 托尼·布莱尔当了10年多的首相。

sentences.en: David Cameron, whose resignation began this period of instability, was prime minister for six years.
sentences.zh: 大卫·卡梅伦（David Cameron），正是他的辞职开启了这段动荡时期，他担任了6年首相。

sentences.en: So what changed? Obvious answer is Brexit.
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么改变了？显而易见的答案是脱欧。

sentences.en: The UK voted to leave the European Union in June 2016, almost exactly 10 years ago, and that revealed some deep divisions in British society.
sentences.zh: 英国在2016年6月投票决定离开欧盟，几乎正好是10年前，这暴露了英国社会的一些深层分裂。

sentences.en: British people disagreed over immigration.
sentences.zh: 英国人在移民问题上意见不一。

sentences.en: They disagreed over what it means to be British, over economic policy, globalization, what kind of country the UK should be.
sentences.zh: 他们在何为英国人、经济政策、全球化以及英国应该成为一个什么样的国家等问题上存在分歧。

sentences.en: And these disagreements didn’t go away after the referendum.
sentences.zh: 而这些分歧在公投后并没有消失。

sentences.en: They became worse. The UK became more divided.
sentences.zh: 它们变得更糟了。英国变得更加分裂。

sentences.en: David Cameron was the prime minister who let the referendum happen.
sentences.zh: 大卫·卡梅伦是允许举行公投的首相。

sentences.en: He campaigned for Britain to stay in the European Union, and then he resigned the morning after the Leave campaign won the vote.
sentences.zh: 他曾为英国留在欧盟而奔走拉票，然后在“脱欧”阵营赢得投票的次日早晨辞职了。

sentences.en: His successor was Theresa May. She promised to deliver Brexit, but after years of negotiations with the EU, she failed to get her Brexit deal approved by the UK Parliament.
sentences.zh: 他的继任者是特雷莎·梅（Theresa May）。她承诺实现脱欧，但在与欧盟进行了多年谈判后，她未能让自己的脱欧协议获得英国议会的批准。

sentences.en: Eventually, members of her own political party lost confidence, and she resigned in 2019.
sentences.zh: 最终，她自己政党的议员失去了信心，她于2019年辞职了。

sentences.en: Boris Johnson was next. He won a huge election victory by promising to get Brexit done, but his government was full of scandals.
sentences.zh: 接下来是Boris Johnson。他通过承诺完成脱欧赢得了一场压倒性的大选胜利，但他的政府丑闻不断。

sentences.en: The most famous scandal was Partygate, where the government held parties during the COVID lockdown for their staff while the public was being told to stay at home.
sentences.zh: 最著名的丑闻是“聚会门”，当时政府在新冠封城期间为其员工举办了派对，而公众却被告知要呆在家里。

sentences.en: Johnson eventually resigned after dozens of ministers, senior politicians, quit his government.
sentences.zh: 在数十名部长和高级政治人物退出其政府后，Johnson最终辞职了。

sentences.en: His replacement was Liz Truss. Liz Truss is famously the worst prime minister in British history, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 接替他的是莉兹·特拉斯（Liz Truss）。莉兹·特拉斯可以说是英国历史上最糟糕的首相。

sentences.en: She lasted just 49 days as prime minister.
sentences.zh: 她仅仅当了49天首相。

sentences.en: Her first policy was massive tax cuts. This caused the UK’s financial markets, actually, the international financial markets, to panic.
sentences.zh: 她的第一项政策就是大规模减税。这引发了英国金融市场、实际上是国际金融市场的恐慌。

sentences.en: The value of the British currency fell, and her government had to abandon all of those plans instantly.
sentences.zh: 英镑贬值，她的政府不得不立即废除了所有这些计划。

sentences.en: She resigned in just 49 days, making her the shortest serving prime minister in British history.
sentences.zh: 她在仅仅49天后就辞职了，这使她成为了英国历史上任职时间最短的首相。

sentences.en: Up next was Rishi Sunak, who inherited a divided Conservative party.
sentences.zh: 接下来是里希·苏纳克（Rishi Sunak），他接手的是一个分裂的保守党。

sentences.en: His political party were really unpopular, and then they suffered a historic defeat in the 2024 election.
sentences.zh: 他的政党极其不受欢迎，随后在2024年的大选中遭遇了历史性惨败。

sentences.en: So after 14 years of Conservative governments, they lost.
sentences.zh: 因此，在经历了14年的保守党政府之后，他们输了。

sentences.en: Next up was Keir Starmer and the Labour Party, but less than two years later, he is resigning as well.
sentences.zh: 接下来是Keir Starmer和工党，但不到两年后，他也辞职了。

sentences.en: And Andy Burnham will be the seventh prime minister.
sentences.zh: 而Andy Burnham将成为第七位首相。

sentences.en: Why has this kept happening? Well, as well as the Brexit referendum, Britain has other challenges.
sentences.zh: 为什么这种情况一直在发生？好吧，除了脱欧公投，英国还面临着其他挑战。

sentences.en: Economic growth is weak. Public services are struggling, and there’s a lot of pressure because the population is getting older.
sentences.zh: 经济增长疲软。公共服务步履维艰，而且由于人口老龄化，压力非常大。

sentences.en: Housing is unaffordable. Politics in the UK is really fragmented at the moment.
sentences.zh: 住房让人买不起。英国目前的政治局势非常碎片化。

sentences.en: For decades, there were basically only two political parties people voted for: Labour, Conservatives.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，人们基本上只有两个政党可以投票：工党和保守党。

sentences.en: But today, people spread their votes across more parties.
sentences.zh: 但今天，人们把选票分散投给了更多的政党。

sentences.en: The Liberal Democrats have done quite well in recent elections.
sentences.zh: 自由民主党在最近的选举中表现相当不错。

sentences.en: The Green Party, the Scottish National Party, Plaid Cymru (the Welsh Nationalist Party), and now Reform UK as well.
sentences.zh: 绿党、苏格兰民族党、威尔士民族党（Plaid Cymru），现在还有英国改革党。

sentences.en: This makes it harder for any leader to build broad support.
sentences.zh: 这使得任何领袖都更难建立广泛的支持。

sentences.en: Social media has also changed politics. Every single mistake the government makes is instantly reported, analyzed, criticized, and shared with millions of people.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体也改变了政治。政府犯下的每一个失误都会被即时报道、分析、批判，并与数百万人分享。

sentences.en: This didn’t happen 30 years ago. If Andy Burnham does become prime minister, one of his biggest challenges will be proving that Britain’s revolving door of prime ministers, Britain’s constant changing of prime ministers, can finally stop.​
sentences.zh: 这在30年前是不会发生的。如果Andy Burnham真的成为首相，他面临的最大挑战之一将是证明英国像旋转门一样的首相更迭、英国不断更换首相的局面终于可以停止了。

sentences.en: Britain is once again getting a new prime minister.
sentences.zh: 英国再次迎来了一位新首相。

sentences.en: Whoever takes over, probably Andy Burnham, will face the same difficult problems that previous prime ministers have faced: slow growth, pressure on public services, rising defense spending, housing shortages, divided politics.
sentences.zh: 无论谁接任，大概率是Andy Burnham，都将面对前任首相们曾面对过的同样棘手的问题：增长缓慢、公共服务压力、不断上升的国防开支、住房短缺、分裂的政治。

sentences.en: Since the Brexit referendum in 2016, the UK has gone through a lot of prime ministers, and each new leader has promised stability, but failed every time.
sentences.zh: 自2016年脱欧公投以来，英国经历了许多位首相，每一位新领袖都承诺带来稳定性，但每次都失败了。

sentences.en: Can Andy Burnham change this? Or is political instability now normal in Britain?
sentences.zh: Andy Burnham能改变这一切吗？还是说政治不稳定现在成了英国的新常态？

sentences.en: Well, I’m not sure. I hope he does well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不是很确定。我希望他能做得好。

sentences.en: I hope he’s a good prime minister for the sake of the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 为了大不列颠及北爱尔兰联合王国的利益，我希望他能成为一个好首相。

sentences.en: But let’s see. Let’s see how he does. But what do you think?
sentences.zh: 但让我们拭目以待。让我们看看他做得怎么样。不过你怎么看？

sentences.en: Are frequent changes in leadership healthy for a democracy?
sentences.zh: 频繁更换领袖对民主制度是健康的吗？

sentences.en: Or do they make it harder for the government to solve problems?
sentences.zh: 还是说这让政府更难解决问题？

sentences.en: Actually, how does your country choose its leader?
sentences.zh: 说实话，你的国家是如何选择其领导人的？

sentences.en: Do you have a prime minister? Do you have a president?
sentences.zh: 你们有首相吗？你们有总统吗？

sentences.en: How often do your country’s leaders change?
sentences.zh: 你们国家的领导人多久更换一次？
